objectives.description: Start two fresh concurrent claude -p sessions, one per project directory
objectives.note: Two independent concurrent pairs run, both confirmed genuinely overlapping by wall-clock timestamp and by a live `ps` snapshot showing both `claude -p` processes present simultaneously with identical elapsed time. Pair 2: BimodalLogic + cslib directly (SESSION3_START/SESSION4_START both 2026-09-09T19:55:17Z) -- this second pair directly reproduces the ORIGINAL reported defect scenario (a session in BimodalLogic alongside cslib).

objectives.description: In each session, call a real lean-lsp tool for BOTH identifiers; own-project resolves, other-project does not
objectives.note: All 4 sessions: mcp__lean-lsp__lean_file_outline on the own-project identifier returned a real JSON outline (populated imports array); on the cross-project identifier it returned 'Error executing tool lean_file_outline: Invalid Lean file path: ... not found in any Lean project (no lean-toolchain ancestor or file does not exist)'. Full verbatim command lines and outputs recorded below in command_log.

objectives.description: Repeat for the cslib-pr648 worktree, which must have been registered automatically by the hook with zero manual steps
objectives.note: Session 2 (this phase) queried cslib-pr648 and resolved correctly. Its registration was never hand-typed by an operator: it was written automatically by lean-lsp-register-project.sh during Phase 4's real end-to-end acceptance test (a genuinely fresh `claude -p "Just report OK"` session with no lean-lsp-specific prompting at all), and Phase 9's later `setup-lean-mcp.sh --project ... --scope project` invocation was confirmed a no-op ('already configured correctly') against that same automatically-written entry -- it did not create or alter it.

notes: lean_file_outline is documented in mcp-tools-guide.md's own 'CRITICAL: Blocked Tools' table as having a known bug (lean-lsp-mcp #115: declarations always come back empty). All four sessions' own-project calls show exactly this shape (declarations:[], total_declarations:null) -- consistent with the documented bug, and irrelevant to what this demonstration measures (file-path/project resolution, not declaration extraction). The cross-project rejection signal (an explicit 'not found in any Lean project' tool error, distinct from an empty-but-successful result) is a structurally different code path from the buggy declarations field and is not affected by that bug.
